_status: FROZEN before any coverage file was read or analysed. Decisions are based only on question wording (revision/scotland/datasets/<q>/questions.json and the closed-question text in parse_qa.json).

stance_collapse.missing: No tick / question not shown => respondent excluded from that stance analysis (never imputed).

minority_definition: Within each analysis, among respondents who have a coverage score for the topic AND a support/oppose label, the smaller of {support, oppose} is the 'minority stance group' and the larger is the 'majority stance group'. Neutral respondents are reported descriptively and excluded from the minority-vs-majority test. Evaluated on the public data only.
primary_selection_rule: For each free-text question, the primary stance variable is the FIRST closed question that (a) the free-text wording links to and (b) has a support/oppose or agree/disagree scale. All other linked closed questions are secondary analyses.

q4.free_text: 4. Please provide any comments you have in relation to the grouping of procedures and the level of regulation required
q4.linked_closed: Q1, Q2, Q3 (procedure -> regulation group); wording 'grouping of procedures and the level of regulation required'

analyses.definition: Q1-Q3 each list procedures that the consultation PROPOSED for Group 1/2/3 respectively. For each procedure answered (excluding Don't know) compare the respondent's chosen group (0 = no regulation, 1, 2, 3) with the proposed group. support = >=50% of answered procedures chosen exactly as proposed; oppose = <50% as proposed (deviates stricter or looser); neutral = only Don't know answers. Direction of deviation is reported descriptively in g_q4_direction only.

q7.free_text: 7. Please provide any comments about the answers you have given to questions 5 and 6

analyses.definition: Q5 collapsed with support_oppose_scale (first question referenced).
Q6 collapsed with support_oppose_scale; labels are the respondent's stance on the literal Q6 proposal ('HIS-regulated practitioners should NOT require a licence'), so polarity is opposite to Q5.

q20.free_text: 20. ... affect anyone based on their protected characteristics
q20.linked_closed: none (impact question; wording links to no stance-bearing closed question)

q21.free_text: 21. ... affect people differently based on their financial situation

q23.free_text: 23. ... and the potential of age restrictions ... rights of children and young people (UNCRC)
q23.linked_closed: Q19 and Q17 (the two closed age-restriction questions; Q18 is not present in the public pages); wording 'potential of age restrictions'

analyses.definition: Q19 'procedures on intimate areas only for clients 18+': Agree=support, Disagree=oppose, I don't know=neutral. Primary because Q17 has no support/oppose scale.
Q17: 'there should be a lower age limit' = support; 'no lower age limit but under-18s treated as Group 3' = oppose; 'I don't know' = neutral.

respondent_type.source: Q25 'Are you responding as an individual or an organisation?' (the only 'About you' categorical field in the public pages; no practitioner/business/member-of-public category exists)

families.primary_stance: official summaries; one test per topic x embedding_model on the primary stance analysis (minority vs majority)
families.secondary_respondent_type: organisation vs individual, per topic x embedding_model
